issues.body: census() classifies every limit == 0 bucket as inapplicable, breached() returns no reasons, and main() therefore treats a payload with zero measured rows as healthy. If an alert is already open, decide([], true) selects close even though the ambient token has no usable bucket and the watchdog has no affirmative evidence of budget health. This violates the stated fail-closed recovery rule. The end-to-end test only asserts that this case emits a census row; it does not assert that it must not close an open alert, and the current decision path would close one.
issues.fix_hint: Represent a valid payload with zero measurable buckets as indeterminate/unhealthy for lifecycle decisions, or explicitly refuse the tick before decide(). Add an end-to-end test using an all-limit-zero payload plus an existing marked alert that asserts no comment/close mutation occurs and a non-success or explicit unreadable/deferred outcome is reported. Keep individual limit-zero buckets inapplicable when at least one other bucket is measurable.
issues.title: An all-inapplicable census can falsely close an active alert

verdict.summary: The watchdog is generally careful about malformed payloads, unconditional census emission, workflow wiring, and failed reads. However, it treats an all-inapplicable payload as affirmative health. When every reported resource has limit 0, census() produces no measured rows and no breach reasons; main() then calls decide([], true) and closes an existing alert. A token with no usable resource bucket has not proved the shared REST budget healthy, so this is a fail-open recovery path. The self-test currently pins that behavior instead of rejecting it.
